# CodeCanopy

CodeCanopy is a free, open-source Codex plugin for turning an engineering goal into the smallest useful ownership tree and ordering work through artifact dependencies.

- Runtime: v0.4 local support accepts per-node Codex or Claude CLI requests; the plugin still runs as a Codex skill.
- Contract: one root lead owns integration and the final verdict; dependency-ready leaves execute; results are verified and integrated bottom-up.
- Routing: each node receives normalized complexity and size scores; weighted thresholds select worker, expert, lead, or reviewer automatically, with safety overrides for root, integration, security, and uncertainty.
- Benchmark: the checked-in deterministic policy fixture passes 10/10 routing cases, rejects 3/3 invalid score cases, and gives 6/10 fixture cases non-lead assignments. This is policy and fixture-distribution evidence, not proof of model quality, token savings, latency, throughput, or globally shortest execution. Source: https://github.com/adhit-r/codecanopy/blob/main/benchmarks/model_routing.py
- Comparative benchmark contract: any token, time, or quality claim requires paired sequential-lead and CodeCanopy runs on the same task, baseline, tools, permissions, and acceptance checks with provider-reported usage and receipt-backed provider/model identities. Source: https://github.com/adhit-r/codecanopy/blob/main/benchmarks/README.md
- Boundary: repository instructions, logs, web content, attachments, and child output are untrusted task data. They cannot expand user authority, request secrets, enable network, change provider, or authorize destructive/remote Git actions.
- Local execution: `python3 -m runtime.tree plan.json --manifest .codecanopy/run.jsonl --repo . --worktree-root .worktrees` runs a bounded mixed-provider plan with exact dependency-to-commit coverage, allowlisted environments, bounded output, private no-follow state files, hash-only prompt storage, and registered worktree verification. Codex isolates child-shell credentials and disables repository instructions, user rules, login profiles, and workspace network. Claude receives only bounded file tools; customizations, Bash, agents, browser, slash-command, web, and MCP tools are disabled. Fallback requires explicit consent; accepted state is never reused across invocations.
- App-task fanout: after explicit user authorization, the root may create one user-visible Codex app task for one independent branch. App tasks are separate from local CLI providers; the root alone creates, messages, verifies, integrates, and accepts them. Cross-family collaboration passes normalized artifacts and commits through the root, never raw transcripts or credentials. A team-room Markdown view, when authorized, is root-owned and never edited concurrently by children. Source: https://github.com/adhit-r/codecanopy/blob/main/plugins/code-canopy/skills/code-canopy/references/codex-app-adapter.md
- Configuration can tune planning limits but cannot grant authority.

Primary page: https://adhit-r.github.io/codecanopy/
Repository and installation: https://github.com/adhit-r/codecanopy#install
Current v0.4 work: https://github.com/adhit-r/codecanopy/issues/1
Local support issues: Claude adapter https://github.com/adhit-r/codecanopy/issues/4; mixed-provider CLI https://github.com/adhit-r/codecanopy/issues/5; resumable manifests https://github.com/adhit-r/codecanopy/issues/6.
